chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Sanctuary (al-Haram) and its signs. He said: 'Indeed, when Adam (peace be upon him) descended to Abu Qubays, he complained to his Lord about loneliness and that he could no longer hear what he used to hear in Paradise. So Allah sent down to him a red ruby, which He placed in the location of the House. He would circumambulate it, and its light would reach the place of the signs. Thus, the signs were taught by its light, and Allah made it a Sanctuary.'

key_terms.اَلْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically the Kaaba in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Kaaba's sanctuary status according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the cosmological significance of the Kaaba by linking its establishment directly to Prophet Adam’s descent, framing the sanctuary as a divine remedy for earthly isolation. The 'red ruby' (Yaquta) serves as both a physical marker and a spiritual beacon, illuminating the boundaries (A'lam) of the Haram, which underscores the Kaaba's role as a focal point for ritual orientation and divine connection in Shia jurisprudence.
